title: Bronze Statuette of Zeus (Jupiter)
subject: Zeus/Jupiter, seated, as lord of the sky
description: A Roman bronze statuette of Zeus (Jupiter), the sky-father. Roman copies preserve the iconography of the Greek Zeus: bearded, seated, often with scepter and thunderbolt.

title: Bronze Bust of Zeus (Jupiter)
subject: Zeus/Jupiter, head and shoulders
description: A bronze bust of Zeus (Jupiter) with the characteristic auburn beard and windswept hair of the classical type.

title: Glass Head of Zeus Sarapis
subject: Zeus Sarapis, the syncretic Greco-Egyptian god
description: A glass head of Zeus Sarapis — a syncretic deity merging Zeus with the Egyptian Osiris-Serapis, popular in the Hellenistic Mediterranean. An example of how Greek gods were fused with foreign ones.

title: Marble Head and Torso of Athena
subject: Athena, helmeted
description: A marble head and torso of Athena in her war-goddess aspect, wearing the helmet. Roman copy after a Greek original.

title: Terracotta Lekythos (Oil Flask) with Athena
subject: Athena on a funerary lekythos
description: A black-figure lekythos (funerary oil flask) painted by the 'Athena Painter' — an example of the distinctive Athenian funerary vase-painting tradition of the 5th c. BCE.

title: Glass Cameo: Bust of Athena
subject: Athena, bust in cameo
description: A glass cameo with the bust of Athena — a Hellenistic/Roman luxury object type depicting the goddess.

title: Panathenaic Prize Amphora (Leagros Group)
subject: Athena Promachos between judges; runners on reverse
description: A Panathenaic prize amphora: Athena Promachos (Athena the warrior) walking between seated judges on the obverse, with an athletic contest on the reverse. These special-state vases were prizes at the Panathenaia festival of Athens.

title: Panathenaic Prize Amphora (Euphiletos Painter)
subject: Athena Promachos; boxers on reverse
description: A Panathenaic prize amphora in black-figure style, with Athena Promachos on the obverse and boxers on the reverse — an example of the oldest phase of the Panathenaic amphora tradition.

title: Bronze Statuette of Poseidon (Neptune)
subject: Poseidon/Neptune, bearded, trident-bearing
description: A Roman bronze statuette of Poseidon (Neptune), the sea-god — bearded, with the trident iconography that identifies him.

title: Bronze Statuette of a God, Possibly Poseidon
subject: Poseidon or a river god (Okeanos-type)
description: A Hellenistic bronze statuette of a bearded god, probably Poseidon or a river god (an Okeanos-type) — bearded river/sea gods share iconography in Greek art.

title: Marble Statue of Hermes (after Polykleitos)
subject: Hermes, the messenger god
description: A Roman marble copy of a 5th-century Greek statue of Hermes by Polykleitos — the messenger god, patron of travelers, commerce, and boundaries.

title: Bronze Herm of Hermes Propylaios
subject: Hermes Propylaios, the 'gatekeeper' Hermes
description: A bronze herm (a pillar topped with a head) of Hermes Propylaios — Hermes as the 'gatekeeper' god of thresholds, the type of herm set at entrances.

title: Marble Statue of Hermes
subject: Hermes, standing
description: A Roman marble statue of Hermes in a classical (Polykleitos-type) pose — the messenger god in his human, athletic aspect.

title: Limestone Statue of Aphrodite Holding Winged Eros
subject: Aphrodite with Eros, the goddess of love with the winged god of love
description: A Hellenistic limestone statue of Aphrodite holding winged Eros — the goddess of love with the personification of erotic love, a popular Hellenistic theme.

title: Basalt Statuette of Aphrodite (Medici type)
subject: Aphrodite, the Medici-type
description: A Roman statuette of Aphrodite in the 'Medici type' — a famous sculptural type of the goddess in a veiled, contemplative pose.

title: Marble Statue of Aphrodite
subject: Aphrodite, the goddess of love
description: A Roman marble statue of Aphrodite — the goddess of love, beauty, and desire, one of the most widely copied figures in classical sculpture.

title: Terracotta Fragment of a Votive Relief: Hades and Persephone
subject: Hades and Persephone (Kore)
description: A terracotta votive relief fragment of Hades and Persephone (Kore) — the underworld king and the queen he abducted. A rare direct depiction of the divine couple.

title: Relief Fragments from the Great Eleusinian Relief
subject: Demeter, Persephone, and Ploutos (the Eleusinian theogony)
description: Marble fragments of the Great Eleusinian Relief: Demeter (the grain-mother) and her daughter Persephone (Kore) with Ploutos (the child-god of wealth) — the central image of the Eleusinian Mysteries.

title: Bronze Mirror with Perseus and the Graiai
subject: Perseus and the Graiai (the Gorgon quest)
description: An Etruscan bronze mirror engraved with Perseus and the Graiai — the hero on his quest for the Gorgon Medusa's head. Etruscan mirrors are a major source for Greek myth iconography.

title: Gilded Silver Relief: Woman, Herakles, Artemis, and a Gorgon
subject: A gorgon (Medusa-type) with Herakles and Artemis
description: A gilded silver relief showing a gorgon (Medusa-type) with Herakles and Artemis — an early example of the Gorgon in Mediterranean metalwork, before the classical Greek period.
